title: Detect and recover from Helm post-install finalizer leaks causing operator reconcile stalls
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several customers on Private/VPC reported operator reconcile stalls after Helm 2.4.0 upgrades. Investigation shows at least two different Helm post-install hooks leave CR finalizers (finalizer field) in a partial state when a race occurs between post-install job cleanup and the operator's reconcile. Finalizer entries referencing ephemeral job resources are never removed, preventing CR deletion and causing aggressive reconcile retries and resource leaks. This ticket covers detection (new alert), safe automatic remediation (hotfix operator behavior to detect and reclaim leaked finalizers), and a controlled hotfix rollout for affected clusters.
reproduction_steps: 1) Install operator chart v2.4.0 into a cluster that already has nodeagent v1.x and a running onprem CR
2) Trigger a chart upgrade with post-install hook that creates ephemeral Jobs which add finalizers to CRs (simulated by helm test hooks)
3) Simultaneously scale down nodeagent to force the reconcile to pause and resume while hook cleanup is ongoing
4) Observe the CR stuck with finalizer entries that reference jobs that no longer exist and operator logs showing repeated reconcile errors about missing owner references
5) Confirm remediation by manually removing the leaked finalizer and observing normal reconciliation resumes
impact_summary: Impacts Private and on-prem customers during operator or chart upgrades. Symptoms include: stuck CRs, increased controller CPU due to tight reconcile loop, helm upgrade failures on subsequent attempts, and potential customer outages when controller cannot reconcile resource lifecycles (eg. nodeagent never completes drain state). Several escalations from enterprise customers with strict upgrade windows.
mitigation_attempts: 1) Manual remediation runbook published: safely remove leaked finalizers and restart operator (DOC link shared with SE team)
2) K8s API-level temporary script pushed to customer clusters by SE to clear orphaned 'helm.sh/hook' refs (used in three escalations)
3) Emergency rollback guidance to previous chart v2.3.9 when rollback path is clean
proposed_fix: Operator hotfix: on startup and during reconcile, detect finalizer entries that reference transient helm Job objects with ownerReferences missing. Add a guarded reclaim path: validate finalizer provenance, annotate CR as 'reclaiming', attempt safe removal of orphaned finalizer entries (with audit log), emit events, and continue reconcile. Add a fallback flag to skip removal in clusters with third-party finalizer constraints. Also add Helm chart preflight probe that detects potential race windows and blocks upgrades with a clear error explaining the required steps.
rollout_plan: Build operator-2.4.1-hotfix with finalizer-reclaim logic behind feature flag 'finalizer_reclaim' (default off for initial rollout)
Stage canary rollout to internal QA and 2 low-impact customer clusters with support on standby
Open communication with impacted customers and offer coordinated upgrade window for hotfix application
If canary stable for 48 hours, flip default flag on for new installs and schedule automated remediation run for known leaked CRs
Patch chart and release stable operator-2.4.1 within 72 hours of merge
acceptance_criteria: Automated unit and integration tests for finalizer reclaim cover common helm hook patterns
Canary clusters show zero recurrence of stuck CRs for 48 hours post-apply
SE-run remediation cleared at least three customer escalations without further manual intervention
Monitoring/alerts created and firing with actionable context for future incidents
testing_plan: Create synthetic clusters in CI that simulate helm post-install job races and validate hotfix removes leaked finalizers safely
Scale tests to ensure operator reconcile throughput unaffected by reclaim path (no more than 5% CPU increase under 95th percentile load)
Run E2E upgrade matrix against nodeagent permutations customers reported (1.x/2.x)
monitoring_playbook: Alert: >5 reclaim attempts in 10m for a single cluster => SE paging (signal of upgrade bug or scripted drift)
Dashboard: table of CRs with 'leaked_finalizers' label and last_seen timestamp; link to customer cluster logs
Audit: centralized event log of finalizer removals with actor, reason, and PR reference
notes: SE escalations timeline: 2026-02-24 first report, 2026-02-26 repeat with another cluster, 2026-02-28 escalating to engineering
We intentionally keep finalizer_reclaim behind a feature flag until we validate no unintended removal of third-party finalizers
Consider adding a Helm lifecycle advisory to chart release notes to avoid simultaneous nodeagent scale-down during post-install hooks
